BattleBots FaceOffs (2024)}}'''Bloodsport''' is a [[Heavyweights|heavyweight]] robot built by [[Bots 'n' Stuff Robotics]], which has fought in every ''[[BattleBots]]'' season since [[World Championship IV]]. It has also competed in all three [[Discovery]] spin-off seasons, as well as untelevised events like [[BattleBots Proving Ground|''Proving Ground'']], ''[[BattleBots FaceOffs|FaceOffs]]'' and the 2026 [[BattleBots Pro League|''BattleBots'' ''Pro League'']]. In its [[World Championship IV|debut season]], Bloodsport was a round, black and red robot armed with a 47" [[Bar Spinners|bar spinner]] with sharpened, blood-spattered edges originally made from S7 tool steel. The robot also had a curved pole protruding from the top, assisting it to [[Self-righting mechanism|self-right]] in a similar fashion to [[Gigabyte]]. Bloodsport was also accompanied by a [[Minibots|minibot]] named '''Thumb War''', which bore a passing resemblance to three-time [[Comedy Central]] ''BattleBots ''champion [[Hazard]]. However, the team took inspiration from [[Icewave]] for the design of their main robot, according to the show. [[File:Bloodsport WCIV hero shot.png|left|thumb|Bloodsport during World Championship IV hero shots.]]The robot was originally a [[Reserves|reserve]], but ultimately competed in the main competition.https://www.bloodsportbattlebot.com/robots/bloodsport-v1 Bloodsport won a decision with [[Lucky]], and chalked up knockout wins against both [[Breaker Box]] and [[The Four Horsemen]]. However, Bloodsport lost to [[Black Dragon]] and failed to make the Top 16 after being deflected out of the [[BattleBox]] during a play-in [[Rumbles|rumble]] with [[Railgun MAX]] and [[Uppercut]]. [[File:Bloodsport WC V hero shot.jpg|left|thumb|Bloodsport during World Championship V hero shots.]] Bloodsport returned for [[World Championship V]], with a new look to the bot, inspired by the team's [[Beetleweights|beetleweight]] '''Zero Traction'''. The bot was heavily different to its first iteration, sporting a low, box-shaped chassis to allow for it to win more pushing battles. Bloodsport also sported a set of four hinged wedgelets at the front and five different weapon bars made from a mix of AR500 and S7 tool steel: the '''Long Bar''', '''The Disk''', the '''Tri-bar''', the '''THICC bar''' and the '''Key''', ranging from 57lbs to 77lbs in weight. The four Scorpion 5025 motors powering the primary weapon of Bloodsport ensured it could hit the 250mph maximum tip speed ''BattleBots ''allows. With the new shape to the chassis, the team had to redesign the self-righting pole to allow for it to remain functional without the four corners hitting the BattleBox floor. The eventual shape ensured this would not happen, and would put less stress on the weapon motors. Bloodsport performed significantly better in the 2020 season, finishing the [[Fight Night]] rounds with an unbeaten 3-0 record, including a [[Main Event]] victory over eventual season champion [[End Game]] - the New Zealand bot's only loss of the season. It won its Round of 32 fight against [[Gruff]], but lost to [[Seems Reasonable Robotics|Aren Hill's]] [[Tantrum]] in the Round of 16. Bloodsport also participated in the [[Beta]] [[BattleBots: Bounty Hunters|''BattleBots: Bounty Hunters'']] bracket, defeating rookie bots [[Aegis]] and [[HiJinx]] before losing to ''BattleBots'' veteran [[Mutant Robots|Donald Hutson]] and [[Lock-Jaw]].
[[File:Bloodsport WCVI hero shot above.png|left|thumb|Bloodsport during World Championship VI hero shots.]]Bots 'n' Stuff Robotics came back for [[World Championship VI]] with Bloodsport, along with a brand new robot called [[Retrograde]]. The team swapped out their S7 tool steel blades for a tougher but softer AR500 steel to avoid snapping their weaponry as they did against [[Gruff]] a year prior. These weapon options were slightly lighter, with their heaviest option now weighing 72lbs. However, Bloodsport was largely outclassed by [[Whiplash]] in their opening fight of the season and suffered a first Fight Night loss since 2019. It then redeemed itself with a knockout win over [[SubZero]] and got the nod from the judges against [[Claw Viper]]. In the Top 32, Bloodsport faced [[Minotaur]] but lost after their newest weapon option, '''Club Sandwich''', broke after sustained attacks from the Brazilian bot. Returning for ''[[BattleBots: Champions I]]'', the team debuted a brand new weapon for Bloodsport designed by Nik Buchholz, named the '''Ferrous Wheel'''.https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X_1ypSSYwJo Bloodsport made it through the bracket, defeating [[Big Dill]], [[Blade]], and [[Blacksmith]], but fell to the gatekeeper [[Skorpios]] in the Sin City Slugfest bracket. [[File:Bloodsport WC VII hero shot.jpg|left|thumb|Bloodsport during World Championship VII hero shots.]]The team confirmed their intention to apply for [[World Championship VII]], first revealing the new design for Retrograde before announcing new members in Brian Boxell, Pearl Grey, Curtis Honeycutt and Ellie Clark. Bloodsport's brand new build, known as 'v3', was revealed during the September 2022 ''National Havoc Robot League'' event and showcased a sleeker look, with weapon electronics now stored above the bar itself, reminiscent of [[Icewave]]. The housing was shaped to resemble a head with angry eyes added to the front. Bloodsport also featured a new system for mounting their wedgelets, which had a tendency to come off during battle in previous seasons. The four short Magmotors which had powered Bloodsport since its first incarnation were replaced with TP brushless motors. Its more compact billet frame meant the weapon now had greater reach than before, and the team stated Bloodsport was generally more powerful thanks to its total redesign.https://www.instagram.com/p/CioT2vYLTVp/ In the same post, the team confirmed their acceptance for the competition. One of Bloodsport's main upgrades ahead of the season was their use of live telemetry, which could provide teal time feedback on the robot's current state, including the temperature of their motors, condition of their batteries and more. They designed another brand new 75lb blade for the competition, made from 1¼" thick AR500 steel and known as the '''Chonk Key'''.https://www.instagram.com/p/CqGBKsSLsbF/ Another weapon option for the season was a 68lb '''Wheel of Misfortune''' made from ½" TruSHIELD steel. Their third option is another key-shaped blade made from AR500 steel, this time ¾" thick and weighing 72lbs, known as the '''Skeleton Key'''. Bloodsport began its season with a brutal knockout loss to [[Copperhead]], but rebounded by winning its next two fights against [[Gigabyte]] and [[ROTATOR]]. Its qualifying rounds were rounded off with a loss by judges' decision to [[Beta]], but Bloodsport did enough to make the Top 32 as the No.19 seed. It fell short to [[Lock-Jaw]] in the Round of 32, however, after being upended despite gaining the initial upper hand. Bloodsport returned for ''[[BattleBots: Champions II]]'', but lost in the first round to [[MadCatter]]. In September 2023, Bloodsport fought [[JackPot]] in [[BattleBots Proving Ground|''BattleBots Proving Ground'']] as part of the ''[[BattleBots: Destruct-A-Thon|Destruct-A-Thon]]'' live show. Ahead of the fight, the team confirmed they would be debuting brand new, custom vulcanized rubber wheels courtesy of a new sponsor.https://www.instagram.com/p/CwBDeSHv-aI/?img_index=1 The chassis and head of Bloodsport itself were also painted white for these battles, and the main robot was accompanied by a 20lb [[Minibots|minibot]] called '''Bloodsquirt'''. In order to make weight for this, the main robot was reduced to 230lbs and according to Justin Marple, the electronics had been totally reworked. Bloodsport finished with a 1-1 record against JackPot, losing their first encounter and winning the second. The previous season's build was sold to ''BattleBots'' fan Tom McAtee, confirming another total redesign ahead of future competitions. Bloodsport was rebuilt to compete at ''[[BattleBots FaceOffs]]'', sporting larger, more powerful weapon motors and ditching the head design. Unoficially known as 'Bloodsport v4', its spinner blades were now made from AR600 steel, as seen previously on robots such as [[SawBlaze]] and could reach up to 250mph. The team had swapped over from twin Newmotor 8025 motors to modified 8038 alternatives from the came brand, helping the weapon reach 34HP at its peak - an increase from 20-30HP according to the team's website.https://www.bloodsportbattlebot.com/robots/bloodsport-v3https://www.bloodsportbattlebot.com/robots/bloodsport-v4 Bloodsquirt did not return. Bloodsport would return again in 2026 for the inaugural ''[[BattleBots Pro League]]'', with the most significant change coming to its weapon system. Bloodsport's weapon motors and controllers, which were were previously housed above the blade, were now mounted within the main chassis. A new blade was also manufactured specifically for [[HUGE]] with sharpened teeth, known as '''Kind of a Big Wheel'''.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6i-4Y0BF6BI Week 2 Behind The Scenes At BATTLEBOTS PRO LEAGUE] Team sponsor SSOB provided ARMOX 600 material to manufacture new 'Long Bar' weapons, though the remainder of Bloodsport's arsenal was still made from AR500 steel.Correspondence between [[User:SFCJack|SFCJack]] and Nik Buchholz in June 2026 Bloodsport Faceoffs.png|Bloodsport in front of the Upper Deck. '''Bloodsport vs. Lucky'''

[[File:Lucky Bloodsport.jpg|left|thumb|Sparks fly as Bloodsport and Lucky collide.]]Bloodsport's first ''BattleBots'' match was against the Canadian veteran, [[Lucky]]. The fight began relatively evenly as although Bloodsport was able to get its weapon up to speed, it was unable to cause meaningful damage to Lucky's front wedge. After a few more hits, Bloodsport's weapon spun down as a result of an overheated motor controller, allowing Lucky to take advantage. Bloodsport managed to stay upright during Lucky's attacks, however, and got its weapon back up to speed, managing to strike Lucky's side with little damage done. Bloodsport's weapon eventually spun down again and Lucky took advantage once more. However, when Bloodsport got its weapon going a third time, they tore into and then tore off Lucky's front wedge, sending it flying out of the arena. As the fight wore on, neither robot was able to gain an advantage and both survived the full three minutes. The judges awarded Bloodsport the unanimous decision, giving it a debut win and a 1-0 start to its [[Fight Night]] campaign. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Black Dragon'''

[[File:Bloodsport Black Dragon.jpg|thumb|Bloodsport gets punted onto its back by Black Dragon.]]Bloodsport was next placed against newcomer from Brazil, [[Black Dragon]]. When the match began, Bloodsport was tossed high into the air near the arena barrier, nearly getting flipped over in the process. Bloodsport landed upright and started to get its weapon back up to speed, but quickly took another hit from its opponent and lost its self-righting pole. Making matters worse, the third hit disabled their weapon, which left them quite vulnerable. Bloodsport took a fourth and final hit that flipped them over. With both possible ways to right itself gone or disabled, Bloodsport was unable to get back into the fight and was counted out, giving Black Dragon the win by knockout. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Breaker Box'''

[[File:Bloodsport vs Breaker Box.jpg|thumb|left|Bloodsport rips off Breaker Box's lifting plow.]][[File:Bloodsport vs Breaker Box 2.jpg|thumb|Bloodsport delivers the final blow to Breaker Box.]]Bloodsport was now up against [[Jim Smentowski]] and his upgraded version of [[Breaker Box]]. Bloodsport started off relatively evenly with Breaker Box as their first hit didn't cause any damage. However, as Bloodsport continued to attack, they hit Breaker Box's weapon arm and pulled it away from the chassis. Additionally, the impact caused Breaker Box some drive issues. Bloodsport then ripped off the entire plow assembly and left Breaker Box with little to fight or defend with. Bloodsport's weapon then spun down for much of the match but Bloodsport had done enough to Breaker Box that there was little for them to deal with. Bloodsport then got its weapon going and delivered a final hit that knocked Breaker Box out. Breaker Box was counted out, giving Bloodsport the win by KO at 1:36. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. The Four Horsemen'''

[[File:Bloodsport hits TheFourHorsemenSkye.jpg|thumb|left|Bloodsport destroys Skye.]][[File:Bloodsport hits TheFourhorsemenPizza.jpg|thumb|Bloodsport hits Pizza.]][[File:Bloodsport hits TheFourhorsemenButtercup.jpg|thumb|left|Bloodsport hits and rips off Buttercup's wheel.]]Up next for Bloodsport was a match against [[Team Bigger Brother|Ian Watts]] and [[The Four Horsemen]]. Bloodsport also brought in its little minibot of Thumb War to even the numbers a bit. As the match got underway, Bloodsport attacked Skye and removed its weapon assembly completely, disabling Skye in the process. Next, Bloodsport attacked Pizza and threw it on top of the [[Screws|screws]], where it could not escape. By this point, only the wedgebots were the working members of The Four Horsemen left so Bloodsport went after Buttercup, which was down to one wheel while Daisy was also pretty much immobilized from Thumb War's blade. While Bloodsport broke the other wheel off Buttercup, then went after Daisy and broke a piece of its only wheel left, leaving it pretty much immobilized. The multibot was counted out, giving Bloodsport the win by KO at 1:09. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Uppercut vs. Railgun MAX'''

[[File:Railgun MAX vs Bloodsport vs Uppercut.jpg|thumb|Bloodsport gets punted out of the arena by Railgun MAX.]]Bloodsport was close to the Top 16, but it had to win a rumble against fellow newcomer spinners, [[Uppercut]] and [[Railgun MAX]]. Bloodsport got its weapon up to speed and traded blows with Railgun MAX while Uppercut stayed back. Unfortunately, Bloodsport then took a big hit from Railgun MAX that launched it out of the arena where it landed upside down. This effectively ended its chances at making the Top 16, but it also crippled Railgun MAX badly for the rest of the match against Uppercut. They both continued fighting until Uppercut knocked out Railgun MAX to earn a spot in the Top 16. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Sharkoprion (Exhibition)'''

[[File:Bloodsport Sharkoprion.jpg|thumb|Bloodsport shreds the upper body of Surrenderbot!.|alt=|left]]Bloodsport also had an exhibition match against veteran [[Sharkoprion]], who was accompanied by minibot Surrenderbot!. As the match began, was slow to get its weapon going. Still, it was able to take a hit from Sharkoprion and attack Surrenderbot!. Soon, it got its weapon going and tore into Surrenderbot! and Sharkoprion, leaving both disabled. '''Bloodsport vs. Skorpios'''

[[File:Skorpios Bloodsport s5 2020.jpg|thumb|Sparks fly as Bloodsport and Skorpios exchange blows.]]Bloodsport's first fight of the season was against [[Skorpios]]. In response, Bloodsport went with their new overhead disk spinner. Bloodsport started off well, dishing out hits to Skorpios, but was soon pushed into the arena barrier and had lost two of the front wedgelets, one of which was from its own disk sheering it off. However, Skorpios had little offense to deal with this as its sawblade was bent in an earlier exchange, so Bloodsport continued its attacks, causing damage to Skorpios' front right side, nearly ripping off the front right plate behind the wedgelet. Bloodsport then let its weapon spin down to cool off briefly before getting nearly delivered to the pulverizer. However, Skorpios was much less mobile by this point and smoke began to pour out. After delivering a final hit, Bloodsport waited for the count-out and took the win by KO. The post-fight analysis showed how Bloodsport lost its wedgelets and that it lost its right front wheel at some point in that battle. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. End Game'''

[[File:End game vs bloodsport s5.jpg|left|thumb|Bloodsport delivers a hit to the front of End Game.]]Next for Bloodsport was a match against Jack Barker and [[End Game]], whom had quickly dispatched of the former champ [[Tombstone]] in their last battle. For this match, Bloodsport came in with two wedgelets and their 'THICC Bar'. Bloodsport immediately began by running away to avoid End Game's box rush, striking back twice before quickly losing its wedgelets. With Bloodsport's weapon stopped for now, End Game took a chunk out near the back right wheel, but when End Game began chasing Bloodsport, End Game found its drive failing pretty quick. Bloodsport got its weapon going again and was sent flying into the corner, dangerously close to being ejected like its last hit with Railgun MAX. Bloodsport recovered, but End Game began emitting smoke and had lost its weapon and weapon belt. End Game was counted out, giving Bloodsport the win by KO. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Chronos'''

[[File:Bloodsportchronos.jpg|thumb|Chronos and Bloodsport eye each other up from the off.]]Bloodsport was now up against the ring spinner [[Chronos]], built by veteran competitor [[Team Chronos|Jerry Serrafin]]. Bloodsport was quickly able to take out Chronos' ring spinner but was unwilling to risk further damage to its weapon so it spun down and tried to attack without it. This resulted in mostly a pushing match with Bloodsport only getting its weapon up to maybe half top speed. Still, they managed to take the fight to a judges' decision, which ruled unanimously for Bloodsport. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Gruff'''

[[File:GruffvBloodsport2.PNG|left|thumb|Gruff nearly flips Bloodsport.]][[File:GruffvBloodsport1.PNG|thumb|Bloodsport pushes Gruff against the wall as Gruff activates its flamethrower.]]As one of the few bots to finish the Fight Night rounds with a 3-0 record, Bloodsport made it into the Round of 32 as the No.2 seed and took on the No.31 seed [[Gruff]] and [[Team Gruff|Sam McAmis]]. Bloodsport was armed with its tri-bar but was off to a very poor start as the first impact with their weapon cost them a third of their tri-bar, leaving it unbalanced. After trying unsuccessfully to still use it, Bloodsport resorted to pushing and lost at least one wedgelet as they were lifted up by Gruff. Bloodsport began controlling the match with just its two wedgelets remaining and took Gruff to the pulverizer, suffering a hit from the hammer itself. Gruff was unable to mount much of an attack so Bloodsport controlled the rest of the match and only lost its last two wedgelets before time ran out. The judges awarded Bloodsport a 2-1 split decision and a spot in the Top 16. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Tantrum'''

[[File:Tantrum is hit by Bloodsport.png|thumb|Bloodsport lands a shot on Tantrum.|alt=]]Bloodsport next faced [[Seems Reasonable Robotics|Aren Hill's]] [[Tantrum]] and its team opted for the 'THICC bar' which saw them beat [[End Game]] earlier in the season. The fight started with Bloodsport attempting to find space to spin up to speed, but Tantrum chased them down. Bloodsport inevitably did spin up, but the first meaningful impact saw their own wedgelets be ripped away. Tantrum was able to tank the glancing hits Bloodsport gave, but persisted in chasing its opponent and prevent it from spinning up to full speed. It then held Bloodsport against the side of the box, getting in underneath and pinning it momentarily. Tantrum's drum was spinning, but had yet to land a punch on Bloodsport. It got underneath Bloodsport again, attempted to hold the No.2 seed against the wall, and then rammed it against the red square's screws. Bloodsport escaped and finally got up to speed, but took a hit from the pulverizer after being coerced into the corner by Tantrum. Aren Hill's machine held Bloodsport under the hammer and allowed it to deliver blows to their self-righting pole, bending it out of shape in the process. With under a minute to go, Tantrum chased Bloodsport around the box and continued to smother its attempts to spin up. A wheel then fell out of Bloodsport, allowing Tantrum to pin it under the opposite pulverizer for the remaining seconds of the fight. Tantrum won by a split decision, and Bloodsport's pursuit of the Giant Nut had come to an end. |- ! style="text-align: center;" | ==='''BattleBots: Bounty Hunters'''=== |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Aegis'''

[[File:148200113 239204571119528 6449550684332962706 n.jpg|thumb|Bloodsport immobilizes Aegis.|alt=|left]]Bloodsport's first fight of its [[Beta]] ''[[BattleBots: Bounty Hunters|Bounty Hunters]]'' bracket came against newcomer [[Aegis]]. Bloodsport was equipped with its four-toothed overhead bar spinner but did not immediately spin it up as the match got underway, as Aegis was not moving well at all. Bloodsport got its weapon going anyway and moved Aegis away from the screws to see if it would help them out. Aegis still did not move and was only able to drive in circles after Bloodsport delivered another hit. Bloodsport continued to attack until Aegis was completely ripped open on at least one side and a count-out began. Aegis was counted out, giving Bloodsport the win by KO and a spot in the next round. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. HiJinx'''

[[File:Bloodsport hijinx bounty hunters.png|thumb|Bloodsport and HiJinx meet in the BattleBox.]]After effortlessly taking down Aegis, Bloodsport's team faced [[HiJinx]] in Round 2 and opted to keep using its four-toothed bar. The first impact was relatively minor, causing no visible damage. However, as the match went on, Bloodsport was starting to gain the upper hand as they were keeping on HiJinx and preventing their opponent's weapon from reaching top speed. Bloodsport then tried to attack again but only managed to clip HiJinx's wheel. This left HiJinx struggling but this did not stop Bloodsport from delivering another hit. This proved to be the final blow as a piece of HiJinx was torn off and HiJinx's weapon was the only part of the robot moving. HiJinx was counted out, giving Bloodsport the win by KO and a spot in the next round of the bracket.

Despite being on the winning end of this match, Bloodsport's team had to retire the chassis due to damage sustained from HiJinx's bar.[https://youtu.be/BQ5qFqsp7zo?feature=shared&t=99 Another BATTLEBOTS FACE-OFF Reveal!!!] |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Lock-Jaw'''

[[File:Bloodsport vs lock-jaw s5.png|left|thumb|Bloodsport aims for the plow of Lock-Jaw.]]Bloodsport was now in the semi-finals to determine which of them would face [[Beta]] for a piece of $25,000. In this fight, they faced veteran [[Mutant Robots|Donald Hutson]] and [[Lock-Jaw]]. Both robots remained active before time ran out but the judges put Lock-Jaw into the finals to face Beta. |- ! scope="col" style="text-align: center;" | ==='''World Championship VI'''=== |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Whiplash'''

[[File:Whiplashbloodsport2021.jpg|thumb|Sparks fly as Bloodsport and Whiplash duke it out.|alt=|left]][[File:Whiplashbloodsport2021(2).jpg|thumb|Bloodsport tries to escape Whiplash.|alt=|right]][[File:Bloodsport vs whiplash s6 3.png|thumb|Bloodsport lays immobile on top of the Upper Deck.|alt=|left]]Bloodsport's first fight of the 2021 season was a [[Main Event]] bout against the previous season's runner-up [[Whiplash]]. Whereas the [[Team Fast Electric Robots|Vasquez family]] were only denied the Giant Nut by [[End Game]] a season prior, Bloodsport was the only robot to beat the New Zealand team en route to their title win. Bloodsport had its tri-bar for this fight and just two inside wedgelets, whereas Whiplash opted for additional armor, sacrificing their disk spinner to remain under the weight limit. The fight began with Whiplash charging straight at Bloodsport to try and prevent them from spinning up, but Whiplash had to turn due to Bloodsport's movement, running into the Upper Deck in the process. Bloodsport dealt some glancing shots with its tri-bar spinner, but was largely running away from Whiplash as it dealt occasional glancing blows with its primary weapon. Bloodsport lost a tire from one of the next engagements and found itself clamped down by the arm of Whiplash and run into the one set of screws, which appeared to not be working. Bloodsport attempted to spin up but was grabbed again and taken to the Upper Deck this time, where it was freed. Despite having the more damaging weaponry, it was Bloodsport who had taken the most damage up to this point. And as it found itself caught momentarily on a killsaw slot, Whiplash capitalized and got underneath Bloodsport, lifting it over. It righted itself but was overturned again, carried over the screws and on top of the Upper Deck, where it could no longer right itself. Bloodsport was counted out, and Whiplash took the win by KO with just a second left on the clock. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. SubZero'''

[[File:Bloodsport subzero s6 2021 1.png|thumb|SubZero lands a flip on Bloodsport.]][[File:Bloodsport subzero s6 2021 2.png|left|thumb|The knockout blow.]]Bloodsport's second fight was against [[SubZero]]. Having found no luck with their tri-bar against Whiplash, the team opted to use their four-toothed bar, while SubZero sported a front wedge to deflect the shots from Bloodsport. When the match began, Bloodsport lost several wedgelets from its early attacks, but also damaged the front of their opponent. SubZero attempted to flip multiple times, though missed several times in succession. By the time they finally landed a flip, but Bloodsport landed upright and was not affected by the attack. However, SubZero appeared lethargic and was being outdriven by Bloodsport, who took the opportunity to land more hits to the front of SubZero. The deadly bar continued to slice into the sides of SubZero, bending side armor into one of its wheels and causing it to begin smoking. As SubZero's rear wheel was still spinning but could not make contact with the floor, it became clear the repeat attacks had warped the chassis enough to high-center SubZero on its own frame. Bloodsport landed one more hit on the immobile SubZero, which sent one of its wheels flying towards [[Chris Rose]]. It was then counted out and Bloodsport took the win by KO. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Claw Viper'''

[[File:Bloodsport Claw Viper.jpg|left|thumb|Bloodsport fighting Claw Viper.]][[File:Claw viper Bloodsport charge s6 2021.gif|thumb|Claw Viper fights back despite losing its weapon.]]Sat at 1-1, Bloodsport was given a third Fight Night battle to determine their tournament fate. Their final opponent was fellow 1-1 bot [[Claw Viper]]. Bloodsport was able to spin up and dealt a glancing hit to Claw Viper's back end. It then turned and drove straight into Claw Viper's weapon, ripping off its top clamping arm and buckling the UMHW forks. Claw Viper gave chase but in trying to lift its opponent, sent its weapon into the spinning bar of Bloodsport. This further damaged Claw Viper's weaponry and a chunk of UMHW was sent flying towards the drivers. The two bots went head to head again, this time sandwiching Hatchling and causing damage to its battery as smoke rose from the minibot. However, Claw Viper was able to use its superior drive power to bully Bloodsport into the short corner and under the pulverizer. It escaped to spin up again and dealt another hit, but Bloodsport was sent flying and almost bounced out of the arena. Claw Viper continued to tank hits from the horizontal spinner as it again got underneath Bloodsport and drove it the length of the BattleBox, slamming it into the housing for the screws, and then into the hazard itself. Bloodsport had again spun up but was lacking a wedgelet and attempted to land attacks in the closing seconds but was unsuccessful. The remains of Claw Viper's weaponry dangled from the bot as the fight went to the judges, and as damage carried more weight, Bloodsport took the win by a unanimous decision, sealing a place in the Top 32 as the No.17 seed. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Minotaur'''

[[File:Bloodsport minotaur 1 s6 2021.png|left|thumb|Minotaur shoves Bloodsport into the corner.]][[File:Bloodsport minotaur 2 s6 2021 .png|thumb|Bloodsport is pinned against the wall late on.]]Bloodsport's first opponent in the knockout stages was [[Team RioBotz]] and No.16 seed [[Minotaur]]. For this battle, Bloodsport debuted their 'Club Sandwich' weapon and opted for just a single hinged wedgelet at the front. Both robots immediately spun up as they evaded each other in the opening seconds. Minotaur then landed a shot on Bloodsport which popped it into the air. Upon landing, it became apparent that Bloodsport's weapon had buckled upward on one side and a piece had come off as it drove away. Despite being unbalanced, Bloodsport spun up again but shook as it did so and was stopped as soon as it hit Minotaur. This happened several times over with Bloodsport unable to cause damage to the frame of the 2018 season runner up. Bloodsport finally got its weapon back up to a high speed and made contact with Minotaur, but again came off worse and was shoved into the Upper Deck. They escaped, but Minotaur attacked from the front and ripped away its single wedgelet. The Brazilian bot remained aggressive as it smothered its opponent, pressing it against the arena barrier. As time wore on, Bloodsport suffered several pulverizer hits but survived as the fight went to the judges. Minotaur took the win by unanimous decision, eliminating Bloodsport from the competition. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Riptide (Exhibition)'''

[[File:Riptide Bloodsport 2021 Exhibition 1.gif|right|thumb|Riptide tries to right itself.]][[File:Riptide Bloodsport 2021 Exhibition 2.gif|thumb|Both robots collide.|left]]Following the conclusion of the season, Bloodsport competed in an exhibition match against [[Riptide]], shown as part of ''Vengeance in Vegas''. Bloodsport sported two long front forks for this battle. Both bots spun up as Riptide dealt the first attack of the match - a glancing blow which saw Bloodsport deflect towards the wall. Bloodsport showed its back end to Riptide and reversed into it, but caused no noticeable damage. Bloodsport then reversed and allowed Riptide to drive into it, which threw Ethan Kurtz's bot over. Riptide lined up and drove at its opponent. Now inverted, Riptide was spinning downwards and the impact sent Riptide twisting into the Upper Deck and landing upside-down again. The rookie bot had lost one of its ears in this attack, and the eggbeater drum now made contact with the floor as it tried to escape to safety and eventually self-righted. Bloodsport spun up again, but slammed its blade into the arena paddle as it tried to deliver a shot, giving Riptide the time to spin its weapon back up to speed. Riptide escaped the short corner and dished out another glancing blow. The next attack flipped both robots over and sent them to opposite ends of the BattleBox. Although Riptide was able to right itself, it lost its other ear. But it was Bloodsport who came out of the exchange worse, as it was now upended and against the drivers' booths. Bloodsport did not have the torque in its weapon to right itself, so encouraged Riptide to attack. [[Team Break32]] obliged, slamming its weapon into Bloodsport, but now neither robot appeared healthy as their weapons slowed to a halt. Both robots engaged in a pushing match in the short corner, which resulted in smoke coming from Bloodsport's motors. Its weapon sprung back to life momentarily, but Riptide smothered Bloodsport and pinned against the BattleBox before pushing it around at will. Bloodsport attempted to spin up again, but Riptide drove into its weapon, which cost Bloodsport one of their forks. Later in the fight, Riptide pinned Bloodsport again and a brief fire began inside Justin Marple's bot before smoke began to show again. Bloodsport got its weapon back up to speed in the final ten seconds of the fight, but both robots were mobile at the end. Riptide took the win by way of a split judges' decision. |- ! scope="col" style="text-align: center;" | ==='''BattleBots: Champions I'''=== |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Big Dill'''

[[File:Big Dill Bloodsport BB Champs.jpg|thumb|Big Dill attempts to get the better of Bloodsport.]]Bloodsport entered the post-season series ''[[BattleBots: Champions I]]'', and met [[Big Dill]] in the first round. Early on in the battle, Big Dill swerved to avoid Bloodsport, keeping its lifter up as Justin Marple's bot got up to speed. Bloodsport got the first big attack in, but Big Dill used its raised forks to guide it towards the screws. However, Big Dill's weapon chain broke as it stopped moving for a moment and Bloodsport was allowed to escape unharmed. It then surged forward, jamming itself underneath the screws, which were unable to reverse. Bloodsport spun back up before tearing the rear panel away from Big Dill, exposing its drive motors. Big Dill was stuck on its weapon chain and was counted out, but not before Bloodsport slammed its blade into Spicy Meatball in an attack which sent the D2 kitbot flying across the BattleBox and into the side of the Upper Deck. Bloodsport advanced to the second round of the bracket. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Blade'''

[[File:Skorpios bloodsport high centered BB Champs.png|left|thumb|Bloodsport leaves Blade beached.]]After a comfortable win, Bloodsport met [[Team ORBY]] and [[Blade]], which had defeated [[Kraken]] in the previous round. Blade driver Sangeun Ju opted to point Blade's rear plow at Bloodsport from the off, deflecting its initial attack. Bloodsport attacked the plow, bending it downwards as a result. This meant Blade's wheels were now off the BattleBox floor and it was unable to move. Bloodsport had bounced away as a result of the exchange, but landed on its wheels and acknowledged Blade was high-centered. Blade was counted out, and Bloodsport moved on. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Blacksmith'''

[[File:Bloodsport ferrous wheel BB Champs.png|thumb|Bloodsport with its new horizontal weapon.]][[File:Blacksmith bloodsport 2 BB Champs.png|left|thumb|Blacksmith takes Bloodsport to the screws.]][[File:Blacksmith Bloodsport late attack BB Champs 3.gif|thumb|Blacksmith's vital error.]]Bloodsport now faced [[Team Half Fast Astronaut|Al Kindle]] and [[Blacksmith]]; the winner would earn the right to face [[Bot Bash Party Crew|Zach Lytle]] and [[Skorpios]]. In this all-important battle, Bloodsport debuted its brand new weapon blade, named the "Ferrous Wheel". In response, its opponent was armed with a front plow rather than the forks which had seen it beat [[Deadlift]] and [[Switchback]]. Bloodsport immediately spun up and left a slice in Blacksmith's plow as it dealt a succession of hits which left it upside-down. Blacksmith righted itself as this exchange also cost Bloodsport one of its two hinged wedgelets. Sparks flew as Bloodsport continued to graze the front of Blacksmith, who continued to tank hits before being spun around and taking a hit to its rear. Bloodsport then bounced up the front of its opponent, leaving a scar down the right side of Blacksmith's AR500 steel armor. Yet to land a shot with its flaming power hammer, Blacksmith kept the weapon prepared for any opportunity to attack. Bloodsport hit the rear of Blacksmith again, who suddenly became caught in the wall. Blacksmith took its opportunity with Bloodsport's weapon now halted, and rained down several overhead attacks directly to the new horizontal disk. Although, Bloodsport escaped relatively unscathed, Blacksmith's momentum continued as it rammed Bloodsport weapon-first into the wall before taking it to the screws. Its power hammer delivered several blows to Bloodsport as it was momentarily beached on the hazard. The screws reversed, but Bloodsport fell wedgelet-first and Blacksmith took advantage, pinning it against the hazard once more. Blacksmith got around to Bloodsport's front again, but as its horizontal spinner got up to speed, Blacksmith mistimed an overhead attack, which destroyed its power hammer. The disk lay useless on the floor and parts scattered the BattleBox as Blacksmith made one last attempt to leave an impression on the judges by shoving Bloodsport into the short corner. In a close fight, a split decision went in favor of Bloodsport. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Skorpios'''

[[File:Skorpios bloodsport BB Champs.png|left|thumb|Skorpios pins Bloodsport against the wall.]][[File:Bloodsport Skorpios BB Champs hit.gif|thumb|Bloodsport takes a hit from Skorpios.]][[File:Skorpios bloodsport BB Champs 2.png|left|thumb|Skorpios uses its weapon to keep Bloodsport at bay.]]Having advanced through the bracket unbeaten, Bloodsport earned the right to face [[Skorpios]], the gatekeeper to the Golden Bolt tournament in a rematch from the [[World Championship V|2020 season]]. Skorpios was the early aggressor, tanking Bloodsport's first attack and chasing it around the BattleBox. As its front armor absorbed another glancing hit, Skorpios got to the side of Bloodsport and threw its disk into its opponent's blade. In a strong showing of control, Skorpios pinned Bloodsport and repeatedly hit it, though notably struggled to spin back up to speed. Bloodsport attempted to get back up to speed itself, but Skorpios coerced it into the corner before ramming it against the screws. Bloodsport finally spun up, dealing a glancing hit before being smothered by its opponent. Bloodsport slowed again and Skorpios took advantage, as it pressed Justin Marple's bot against the barrier in front of both teams. Skorpios brought its arm towards Bloodsport's horizontal weapon, but neither spinner was active at this stage. It eventually escaped, and found the space to get its horizontal weapon up to speed once more. Skorpios drove at Bloodsport, but suffered a side swipe to its articulating arm, which bent it slightly to one side. Skorpios tried to power its disk again, but it kept stopping and the arm itself appeared unable to retract as it lay limp on top of Bloodsport's horizontal disk and sparks flew. Skorpios remained aggressive in spite of this, pinning Bloodsport once more. Although Bloodsport had caused the bulk of the damage, it was chased into the screws of the Upper Deck and eventually found itself atop the hazard. Unlike in its Fight Night loss to Whiplash, Bloodsport managed to escape, but found itself in the clutches of Zach Lytle's bot in the final seconds of the match. Both robots were active at the end, and Skorpios took the win by way of a 2-1 split judges' decision. As such, Bloodsport failed to make the Golden Bolt tournament. |- ! scope="col" style="text-align: center;" | ==='''World Championship VII'''=== |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Copperhead'''

Bloodsport's first Fight Night opponent of World Championship VII was against [[Copperhead]], now under the captaincy of [[Caustic Creations|Luke Quintal]]. For this battle, Bloodsport debuted its new weapon, the "Chonk Key".

[[File:Bloodsport Copperhead WCVII.jpg|thumb|180px|Bloodsport and Copperhead in the BattleBox.]][[File:Bloodsport Copperhead WCVII (2).jpg|thumb|180px|Bloodsport turns to face Copperhead.|left]]As Bloodsport got up to speed, it veered right before reversing to avoid Copperhead's drum spinner. It turned to face Copperhead, who dealt a devastating shot which sent both robots careening to different corners of the BattleBox. Copperhead swiftly recovered, but Bloodsport came out of the exchange considerably worse. The impact caused its self-righting pole to detach from the robot and destroyed the Nylon box containing the speed controllers for Bloodsport's weapon.

[[File:Bloodsport Copperhead KO WCVII.png|thumb|Bloodsport lays immobile.]]As Justin Marple's bot lay dormant with a drive chain dangling limply, a fire erupted from within and Bloodsport was promptly counted out. Copperhead took the win by knockout in under 40 seconds to go to 1-0. {{Quote|Chonk Key so powerful but our head assembly's ESC containment was only 3D printed Nylon... Wires ripping and all that kind of chaos, the ESCs exploded shortly after.|Pearl Grey elaborates on the damage caused to BloodsportPublic message from Pearl Grey in the Out of the Arena Discord server}} [[File:Copperhead damaged frame rail vs Bloodsport WCVII.jpg|left|thumb|154x154px|Copperhead's damaged frame rail, courtesy of Bloodsport.]]Copperhead did not come out of the fight unscathed either, as Luke Quintal revealed its frame rail had been warped out of shape on impact and had to be retired.Public message from Luke Quintal in the Out of the Arena Discord server |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Gigabyte'''

[[File:Bloodsport wheel of misfortune vs Gigabyte WCVII.png|thumb|Bloodsport equipped with its Wheel of Misfortune weapon disk.]]Bloodsport's second Fight Night battle was against fellow 0-1 bot [[Gigabyte]]. With neither wanting to slip to an 0-2 record, Bloodsport was equipped with the 68lb 'Wheel of Misfortune', armed with large, twin teeth designed to bite into its opponent's shell.

[[File:Bloodsport Gigabyte WC VII teaser.jpg|left|thumb|Both robots collide with thirty seconds gone.]]Bloodsport immediately chased its opponent down, refusing to allow it any time to spin up to speed, knocking into Gigabyte but opting against firing up its own primary weapon in the meantime.
{{Quote|I have no idea what Justin Marple is thinking here, unless there was something wrong with the weapon...|Kenny Florian as Bloodsport is yet to spin up}}
[[File:Bloodsport Gigabyte WC VII hit.gif|thumb|Gigabyte flips Bloodsport over.]]Gigabyte eventually had its shell spinning and looked to land the first big hit of the battle, but instead grazed against Bloodsport before overturning it. Before Bloodsport had the chance to right itself, Gigabyte dealt a follow-up shot which knocked it away and back onto its wheels. The No.2 seed from [[World Championship V]] escaped and belatedly began spinning its "Wheel of Misfortune", but now Gigabyte was up to full speed too. The weapons collided, sending both robots careening to opposite corners of the BattleBox. {{Quote|Bloodsport closes the distance, but can either robot spin back up, Kenny?|Chris Rose following the massive collision}}
[[File:Gigabyte Bloodsport 4 WCVII KO.png|left|thumb|Bloodsport finishes off its opponent.]]Gigabyte struggled to escape the short corner as Bloodsport recovered and approached the shell spinner, whose weapon was no longer functional. Bloodsport patrolled the corner, but had its front bent downward and lifting the front wheels off the floor slightly.Public comment from Pearl Grey in the Out of the Arena Discord server However, it was still able to land a glancing shot to Gigabyte's shell as one of its drive belts lay on the arena floor. Gigabyte tried to move but quickly ground to a halt and was counted out, signalling Bloodsport's first win of the season. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. ROTATOR'''

Bloodsport's third Fight Night match was a Main Event against former quarter-finalist [[ROTATOR]]. For this draw, Bots 'n' Stuff Robotics equipped it with the conventional 'Long Bar'.

[[File:Rotator vs bloodsport wcvii.png|thumb|Pieces fly off as ROTATOR and Bloodsport come together.]]Bloodsport, the faster of the two competitors, crossed over the left killsaw slots as ROTATOR approached plow-first. Proceeding to dodge its opponent's maneuvers, it circled around and struck ROTATOR from the left side, sending it into a 360-degree aerial spin. This attack bent the left wheelguard of [[Team Revolution|Victor Soto's]] machine open, while leaving it with seemingly reduced mobility.{{Quote|That 72lb weapon - and dishin' out some punishment, right from the get-go! ROTATOR looks stunned a little bit, Kenny.|Chris Rose as Bloodsport damages ROTATOR's wheelguard}}In its pursuit, Bloodsport hopped over the killsaw slots and reversed towards the center of the BattleBox. Turning left, it charged into and engaged in a weapon-on-weapon collision with ROTATOR which sent both competitors recoiling; Bloodsport to the bottom-right killsaw slots, and ROTATOR towards the top-right corner.

[[File:Rotator vs bloodsport wcvii 1.png|left|thumb|Bloodsport is propped against the Upper Deck.]]Bloodsport quickly re-entered the fray, tanking multiple hits from ROTATOR's undercutter while continuing to graze its opponent's front end. Moments later, it delivered another powerful blow - this time to ROTATOR's right-hand side – which was enough to temporarily lift itself off the floor. Two more hits to ROTATOR's left and front followed in rapid succession. However, the second of these knocked Bloodsport back into the spiked bumper, which temporarily halted the momentum of its 'Long Bar'. ROTATOR gave chase as Bloodsport retreated towards the Upper Deck. Another collision between the two competitors threw Bloodsport onto one of the Deck screws, where it was left stranded for several moments. {{Quote|Bloodsport's hung up, ROTATOR has it on the ropes!|Chris Rose, shortly after Bloodsport gets stranded on an Upper Deck screw}}
[[File:Rotator vs bloodsport wcvii 2.png|thumb|Bloodsport hits ROTATOR again.]]While Chris Rose noted that Bloodsport was 'hung up' on the hazard, ROTATOR's mobility was hampered, giving Bots 'n' Stuff enough time to try and free it without risking further damage. While being jostled around by the rotating screw, however, it remained vulnerable, as ROTATOR eventually clipped one end of the 'Long Bar' with its own undercutter. Using the same bar to lever itself sideways, Bloodsport eventually broke free, deflecting a blow from a nearby ROTATOR before heading to the bottom-left perimeter. As the 'Long Bar' regained full momentum, it maneuvered across the BattleBox and into the front of ROTATOR once again. {{Quote|They have space and - looks like ROTATOR might be strugglin' there! This is a great opportunity for Bloodsport! ROTATOR is hurt!|Kenny Florian as Bloodsport pummels a faltering ROTATOR}}
[[File:Rotator vs bloodsport wcvii ko.png|left|thumb|ROTATOR is knocked out.]]Both competitors recoiled, with Bloodsport quick to resume its attacks on a struggling ROTATOR. In these, it caused ROTATOR to lose drive to its left wheel, along with the use of its undercutter. More sparks and debris flew as Bloodsport's 'Long Bar' continued hitting ROTATOR's plow, front-right corner and left wheelguard. The last of these hits immobilized ROTATOR completely, with Kenny Florian also observing damage to the latter's left tire. While Bloodsport lost its own faceplate in the process, it maneuvered across the BattleBox and soon parked opposite ROTATOR, anticipating its opponent's count-out. {{Quote|I think that's gonna be it for ROTATOR. What a win this would be!|Kenny Florian, shortly after Bloodsport immobilizes ROTATOR}} After one minute and 47 seconds, the end buzzer sounded, confirming Bloodsport's second consecutive knockout win of the season. Bots 'n' Stuff Robotics celebrated, having elevated its Fight Night record to 2-1 with the championship bracket looming closer. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Beta'''

Bloodsport's fourth and final Fight Night opponents were [[Team Hurtz]] and [[Beta]], also looking to improve on their 2-1 record. In this battle - considered crucial in determining seedings for the Round of 32 - it was again armed with its "Wheel of Misfortune", along with a set of smaller front wedgelets.

[[File:Beta Bloodsport WCVII slam.gif|thumb|Bloodsport is slammed into the screws.]]From the outset, Bloodsport was pursued by Beta, first making its way across the bottom inner perimeter and into the center. Turning round, it weaved into and sent sparks flying from Beta's heavily-armored wedge, but was soon pushed and chased around by the UK entry. Bloodsport's wedgelets caught the bottom-left killsaw slots, allowing Beta to get underneath and slam it into the bottom-left paddle. Launching into the air on impact, Justin Marples' machine landed on its wheels, successfully dodging Beta's first hammer attack.

[[File:Beta Bloodsport WCVII 1.png|left|thumb|Beta presses Bloodsport against the Upper Deck.]]Bloodsport, however, spun round and was collected by Beta again, finding itself being driven into one of the red square screws. The impact almost flipped it over, but again Bloodsport tumbled back onto its wheels, only to be scooped up and steered into the other screw on the same side. Beta pushed Bloodsport into the Upper Deck bumper, halting its "Wheel of Misfortune" temporarily. In its attempt to escape, Bloodsport took a hammer blow to its directional indicator and bumped into one of the red square screw mounts. {{Dialogue a-b|Chris Rose|Nice job by Beta using the BattleBox and throw at Bloodsport, right off the rails - and again, off the screws!|Kenny Florian|Yeah, it's definitely doin' a great job at introducing the BattleBox to Bloodsport here. This is exactly what they need to do. They have it trapped in the corner, but Bloodsport escapes!|As Beta shepherds Bloodsport into the top-left pocket}}[[File:Beta Bloodsport WCVII Upper Deck.gif|thumb|Bloodsport is flung atop the Upper Deck.]]The escape allowed Justin Marple and his team enough time to get the "Wheel of Misfortune" back up to full speed. Even so, Bloodsport continued to be hounded by Beta, whose next deflections twice lifted it off the BattleBox floor. The second deflection destabilized Bloodsport, the gyroscopic forces of its disk carrying it into the bottom-right Upper Deck screw. Beta rushed in as Bloodsport tried to back away from the screw. This drive lifted Bloodsport onto its side through gyroscopic procession; the "Wheel of Misfortune" clipped the floor and screw, flinging the entire robot onto the Deck itself.

Bloodsport landed upright and gingerly crept off the Upper Deck platform. As it did so, Beta closed in and hammered it twice, as a sheet of bent metal was dislodged and spun out from underneath Bloodsport's chassis. Bloodsport drove away, hopping over the bottom-left killsaw slots in another attempt to evade Beta's pursuit.
{{Quote|Justin Marple has been able to find space to spin up, but look at the hammer bot tracking him down...|Kenny Florian as Bloodsport tries - in vain - to outdrive Beta once more}}[[File:Beta Bloodsport WCVII 2.png|left|thumb|Beta positions itself before striking with its hammer.]]Again, it was collected, deflected and rammed, this time into the bottom-left corner. While avoiding another blow from Beta's hammer, it was quickly hounded and lifted onto its side while being steered back to the Upper Deck screws. Bloodsport's weapon clipped the left-most screw mount, leaving it defenseless as Beta pinned it against the screw itself, then began hammering both the "Wheel of Misfortune" and the top housing for its internals. Following gentle nudging, Beta backed away, allowing Bloodsport to escape and again spin its disk back up.
{{Quote|Big picture and enormous fight for both these bots sitting at 2-1. You're talking about Round of 32 seeding, and Beta just delivering shots, and stopping the blade of Bloodsport!|Chris Rose, as Beta pounds and releases Bloodsport}}[[File:Beta Bloodsport WCVII 3.png|thumb|Bloodsport in the short corner.]]Bloodsport headed back to the red square, charging into the front of an approaching Beta. This set up another ramming attack by Beta as the match entered half-distance, throwing Bloodsport onto its side against the bottom-left bumper. Bloodsport was promptly released, but was again chased and deflected into the Upper Deck screw mount by Beta. This was followed by two more similar series of attacks by the British hammer bot, both ending in Bloodsport being pushed into the Upper Deck bumpers and screws. Two more rams popped Bloodsport into the air, prompting Beta to push it into the upper-right pocket. Similarly to before, Bloodsport was hammered and pushed up against the center Upper Deck screw mount. {{Dialogue a-b-a-b|Chris Rose|...there you go, Kenny! Justin Marple startin' to square up!|Kenny Florian|And Chris, when Bloodsport gets up on the wedge like that, they are just '''inches''' away from clipping Beta's hammer mechanism.|[after Beta deflects Bloodsport upwards] Jeez!|All that would take is one shot from their blade to '''immediately''' change the tide here. They've '''got''' to keep attacking!|As the battle enters its final minute}}[[File:Beta Bloodsport WCVII Hammer Shots.gif|left|thumb|Bloodsport suffers damage to its weapon housing.]]A relentless Beta began shepherding Bloodsport across the arena again, Bloodsport struggling for control as it spun over the rising [[Killsaws|killsaws]]. Another connection with Beta's wedge occurred at the same time, though Bloodsport was again steered into the bottom-left bumper. The recoil pushed it back up against Beta's wedge, where it took a hammer blow bending its directional indicator. Bloodsport escaped, only to be steered into the Upper Deck corner bumper and top-left paddle, then the yellow bumpers on either side of the BattleBox. Now opposite the control booth, Bloodsport was pinned in place while taking hits to its "Wheel of Misfortune" and top housing from Beta. Though able to push Beta back over the killsaws, the front casing for Bloodsport's weapon housing was hacked apart during these attacks.

Once both robots became separated, Bloodsport headed back to the center, attempting to spin its weapon up before Beta bumped into it. With ten seconds remaining, it was deflected and steered into the bottom-left bumper one last time, but released just before the end buzzer sounded. Though both robots had lasted the full three minutes, Justin Marple commented to his Bots 'n' Stuff teammates about Beta's speed and mistake-free driving. {{Dialogue a-b|Chris Rose|Both bots were fully functional at the end of this match, but it kind of felt like Beta dictated the action from start to finish.|Kenny Florian|No doubt. '''Bloodsport vs. Lock-Jaw'''

[[File:Bloodsport pre lock-jaw WCVII.png|thumb|right|Bloodsport ahead of the fight.]]Bloodsport entered the Round of 32 as the No.19 seed. Fighting the No.14 seed [[Lock-Jaw]], it looked to avenge its loss against the [[Mutant Robots]] machine in ''[[BattleBots: Bounty Hunters]]'', equipped solely with the 72lb 'Long Bar'. According to Chris Rose, Justin Marple intended to learn from his previous mistake, prioritizing a 'more patient' approach over trying to achieve a quick knockout win. {{Quote|It's the grizzled vet, versus the heaviest-hitting horizontal in the field. The winner moves on to the Round of 16.|Chris Rose, shortly before the Lock-Jaw/Bloodsport rematch begins}}[[File:Lock-Jaw WCVII Bloodsport 1.png|left|thumb|Bloodsport's bar makes contact with Lock-Jaw's tire.]]At first, both robots sized each other up in the center, with Bloodsport performing a two-point turn to attack Lock-Jaw backwards. Slamming into its opponent's shock-mounted plow, it slashed the right-rear tire of Lock-Jaw, before darting across the BattleBox to lure it around. A second collision deflected Bloodsport upwards, though Bloodsport kept hitting Lock-Jaw's plow and repeated the same process. Another brace of head-to-head collisions followed; sparks flew as Bloodsport's blows were absorbed by Lock-Jaw.

[[File:Bloodsport Lock-Jaw WCVII 1.gif|thumb|A small fire erupts within Bloodsport as it strikes Lock-Jaw.]]The second of these collisions sent Bloodsport recoiling to the right-hand side of Lock-Jaw. This allowed it to cause further damage to both tires from that side, while sending Donald Hutson's machine spinning away. Flames burst through Bloodsport's weapon housing and from beneath the baseplate during these moments, suggesting that the deflections had caused parts of its own internals to catch fire.
{{Dialogue a-b-a-b|Chris Rose|That's a 72lb blade, and UH-OH!|Kenny Florian|Uh-oh!|We've got flames comin' out of Bloodsport!|There's a good chance, now that that weapon has slowed down, but LOOK at the wheels on Lock-Jaw!|As Bloodsport briefly sets itself alight while slashing Lock-Jaw's tires}} Seemingly unaffected by the flames, Bloodsport immediately attacked Lock-Jaw's plow again, only for the spinning bar to temporarily stop moving. Justin Marple's machine turned and drove front-first into Lock-Jaw, but rode up the front of its opponent while taking two direct hits from its own bar spinner. '''Bloodsport vs. JackPot (9/9/2023)'''

[[File:Bloodsquirt Bloodsport Proving Ground 2023.png|thumb|Bloodsquirt ahead of the first battle.|162x162px]]Bloodsport returned for [[BattleBots Proving Ground|''BattleBots Proving Ground'']] in September 2023 as part of the live show, ''[[BattleBots: Destruct-A-Thon]]''.

[[File:Bloodsport vs Jackpot 1 1.gif|left|thumb|Bloodsport and JackPot collide.]]The fight started off with bot robots taking their time to spin up their weapons. [[File:Bloodsport vs Jackpot 1 2.png|thumb|JackPot hits the underside of Bloodsport.]]JackPot was now inverted and used its self-righter to get back on its wheels. [[File:Bloodsport vs Jackpot 1 KO.png|left|thumb|Bloodsport is counted out.]]While Ace struggled to free Bloodsport, Justin Marple's bot was eventually counted out, causing JackPot to win the fight by knockout after just a minute. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. JackPot (9/10/2023)'''

Bloodsport fought [[JackPot]] for a second time over the weekend.

[[File:Bloodsport Jackpot PG 9-10 1.png|thumb|The big hit between both robots.]]Bloodsport opened with a charge to the opposite side of the box, before turning to engage JackPot, landing a glancing blow. Bloodsport then went weapon to weapon and bouncing away before going head on once again, this time causing both robots to be sent flying across the box. [[File:Bloodsport Jackpot PG 9-10 2.png|thumb|Bloodsport drives JackPot into the screws.|left]]Bloodsport would then go in and destroy one of JackPot's minibots before landing another shot, this time to one of JackPot's rear wheels, sending JackPot into a corner. '''Bloodsport vs. Switchback'''

Competing in ''BattleBots FaceOffs'', Bloodsport's first group opponent was [[Switchback]].

[[File:Bloodsport Switchback FaceOffs 1.gif|thumb|Both bots come together.]]Bloodsport drove towards the drivers' booths as Switchback approached, leading with its rear wedge as it sought to use the horizontal spinner's own power against it. Bloodsport's bar made contact with Switchback's back, overturning [[Team Midnight Invention|Greg Needel's]] machine while throwing Bloodsport into the wall but landing upright.

Switchback promptly self-righted before Bloodsport could deal a follow-up blow to its underside. As it swung its weapon system forward, Switchback's eggbeater spun downward as it dealt an overhead attack to Bloodsport frame. It was unable to capitalize on this, however, as the gyroscopic forces from Switchback's weapon tipped it over.

[[File:Switchback Bloodsport 2 FaceOffs.gif|thumb|Switchback makes a fatal error.|left]]This time, Switchback struggled to recover on its own accord, so Greg Needel asked his opposition to hit him again to try and prolong the battle. Bloodsport's team obliged, slamming into Switchback's eggbeater and sending the robot sliding across the arena.

[[File:Switchback Bloodsport KO FaceOffs.png|thumb|Bloodsport stares down the immobile Switchback.]]Bloodsport positioned itself just outside the red starting square as its opponent's team realised their weapon arm was no longer functional. A count followed, marking a win by knockout for Bloodsport and its team.

Post-fight, Justin Marple elaborated on Bloodsport's reduced weapon power in the second half of the fight as a damaged speed controller meant the bar was only powered by a single motor. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Terrortops'''

Bloodsport next took on [[Terrortops]], which also won its opening battle. The team resolved their speed controller issues in The Pits.

[[File:Bloodsport Terrortops 1 FaceOffs.png|left|thumb|Bloodsport is held against the rails early on.]]Bloodsport quickly got its blade up to speed and swiped the front wedge of Terrortops, but found itself cornered as its opponent showed little fear, opting to start aggressive with its lifter fully back. Terrortops was able to destabilize the horizontal spinner, getting in underneath and battering against Bloodsport's frame in the opening moments of the battle.

[[File:Terrortops JackPot FaceOffs 2.gif|thumb|A big impact sends both robots flying.]]After riding over the top of its opponent, Bloodsport's bar returned to speed in spite of a rear attack from [[Team Terrortops|Ben Burton]] and [[Team Terrortops|Sophia Musk-Burton's]] bot. Bloodsport was flung into the Upper Deck thanks to Terrortops' next hit, swiping the defensive plow of Terrortops again and following through by snapping away some of Terrortops' skeletal top armor. Bloodsport reversed into its onrushing opponent in an attack which spun Terrortops around but propelled Bloodsport across the length of the BattleBox, landing upright but not before slamming into the wall.

[[File:Terrortops JackPot FaceOffs 3.gif|left|thumb|Both bots collide again, breaking Terrortops' weapon and Bloodsport's self-righting pole.]]Both machines turned to face one another again, meeting head-on and again throwing each other to opposite ends of the arena. This attack seized Terrortops' blade and loosened its ablative armor, but also deformed the self-righting pole of Bloodsport. This came off completely as Justin Marple's machine bounced into the Upper Deck, but his team sensed an opportunity with its opponent's disk dead less than a minute into the fight.

[[File:Terrortops JackPot FaceOffs 4.png|thumb|Bloodsport is pinned by Terrortops.]]Terrortops tried to control Bloodsport as damage began to rack up on its front plow, retracting the lifter but opting against feeding it into Bloodsport's horizontal spinner. It was able to achieve this seconds later, however, using the lifter as a clamp to pin Bloodsport against the Upper Deck as it became evident that earlier attacks had totally deformed the bulkheads for Terrortops' vertical spinner. Terrortops then fully lowered its lifter for the first time in the battle, sensing that a flip or fortuitous deflection could render Bloodsport immobile.

[[File:Terrortops JackPot FaceOffs 5.gif|left|thumb|The decisive hit sees Bloodsport flipped.]]Approaching the halfway mark, Bloodsport had lost a wedgelet as well as its self-righter, but was ahead on damage. Bloodsport's team knew they had to continue attacking, bouncing awkwardly as the horizontal spinner was hounded by Terrortops in the following thirty seconds. With a minute remaining, Bloodsport and Terrortops met head-on once more, but this time, Bloodsport was thrown upside-down and landed inverted. While Terrortops spun to celebrate, Bloodsport spun wildly on what remained of its pole, showcasing impressive gymnastics but struggling to return the bot to its wheels.

[[File:Terrortops JackPot FaceOffs 6.gif|thumb|Bloodsport flails helplessly.]]Terrortops patiently held back to wait for the count, which commenced with under twenty seconds remaining. Bloodsport continued to spin beyond the knockout call, but its first loss of the group was confirmed. Despite the result, Justin Marple spoke highly of the fight backstage, labelling it "really, really fun" and "one of the best fights" the team had participated in. |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Fireball'''

Bloodsport's third and final opponent was the team's own [[Fireball]]. For this match, Blodsport opted for its 'Chonk Key' bar and ran without its front wedgelets. Before the match captain Justin Marple extolled the relationship between the two teams and expressed confidence in his robot, saying they just needed to dial in little things to get the bot to its true potential.

[[File:Bloodsport Fireball FaceOffs 1.gif|left|thumb|Both robots exchange early shots.]]At the start of the match, Bloodsport moved towards the corner of the arena, turning its back and letting Fireball make the first attack. The collision sent Fireball careening across the arena, but it retaliated with a huge attack that sent Bloodsport flying into the air, landing next to the Upper Deck. Bloodsport retreated, getting its spinner back up to speed as Fireball came after it. Although Bloodsport was sent flying by numerous hits, including one that caused it to bounce over a pulverizer, it continued to batter away at its opponent.
{{Quote|Sorry, was it something I said?|Steve Judkins as Bloodsport throws a chunk of Fireball at him}} [[File:Bloodsport Fireball FaceOffs 2.gif|thumb|Bloodsport strikes Fireball but ricochets awkwardly across the arena.]]After one significant blow which ripped off one of Fireball's front wedges, Bloodsport took a shot from the pulverizer. Fortunately, its fellow Bots 'n' Stuff Robotics machine was unable to capitalize, as its weapon had stopped spinning and smoke had begun to billow out of the robot. Bloodsport delivered another major hit, then followed up with a massive blow just as Fireball's weapon began to function again. This sent both robots ricocheting to opposite ends of the arena, and caused Fireball to burst into flames.

[[File:Bloodsport Fireball FaceOffs KO.gif|left|thumb|Bloodsport puts an end to Fireball.]]Bloodsport moved in for the kill, slamming Fireball and tearing up its wheels, leaving the eggbeater bot unable to drive. Justin Marple, at the encouragement of his friends on the Fireball team, continued attacking, attacking both its opponent and the arena walls multiple times until the countout was complete.

Bots 'n' Stuff Robotics celebrated the win, as well as the explosive fight, on both sides of the arena as Bloodsport finished the weekend 2-1. |- ! style="text-align: center;" | ===BattleBots Pro League (2026)=== |- |

'''Bloodsport vs. Minotaur'''

Bloodsport made its return for the 2026 ''BattleBots Pro League'', where it faced World Championship III runner-up, [[Minotaur]] in a rematch from World Championship VI. It was again armed with its 'Chonk Key' blade.

Justin Marple's bot began by evading its onrushing opponent, dealing a glancing blow to the frame of Minotaur and bouncing away into the blue starting square. Bloodsport's weapon was halted momentarily by the screws and was unable to return to full speed before Minotaur driver [[Team RioBotz|Daniel Freitas]] unbalanced it with a hit of its own, also managing to tear into one of Bloodsport's back tires. Minotaur gave chase but oversteered into the path of Bloodsport's blade, sending the Team RioBotz machine spinning into the arena wall.

Minotaur recovered quickly and poisted itself to retaliate, delivering a weapon-on-weapon attack which threw Bloodsport several feet both in height and lengthways into the corner of the arena. Two of Bloodsport's rear tires were now damaged, contributing to the horizontal spinner being unable to drive freely. Minotaur lined itself up for another attack, throwing Bloodsport onto the housing beside the blue square's screws.

Though Bloodsport was able to escape, it sat barely mobile near the center of the arena as the Brazilian bull charged once more, hitting its opponent and leaving it to prove it still had sufficient mobility.

[[File:Bloodsport caught on cables Minotaur Pro League.png|left|thumb|Bloodsport immobile in the corner - note the loose cables surrounding it.]]However, an earlier attack in the fight had caused cables - purposefully fitted in a grid-like pattern to the top of the arena to theoretically prevent debris from damaging the roof's lighting - to dangle loosely and lay strewn across the arena floor. Due to engagement rules, Team RioBotz reluctantly attacked again, knocking Bloodsport further into the corner. By this point, Bloodsport's drive system had become partly entangled by the cables. Referee [[David Sanfilippo]] started his count, confirming Minotaur's win by KO after 111 seconds.

Post-fight, it was revealed by several teams in attendance that this fight was paused to try and untangle Bloodsport, but this proved unsuccessful. According to Bots 'n' Stuff Robotics' Seth Schaffer, Daniel Freitas expressed concern at being forced to continue engaging with Bloodsport due to the [https://battlebots.fandom.com/wiki/World_Championship_VII#Engagement_and_Unsticks rules concerning engagement] as had their drum spinner had become entangled by the cable, this could have caused extensive damage to their weaponry.[https://discord.com/channels/651601084019900483/809971550937808926/1529962575285059714 Public comment by Seth Schaffer in the NHRL Discord server] He also revealed miscommunication led to ''BattleBots'' officials originally believing the wire came from Bloodsport. This pause in the fight was ultimately cut from the final episode, as was almost all mention of the [https://battlebots.fandom.com/wiki/BattleBots_Controversies#Bloodsport_vs._Minotaur controversy].
{{Quote|We were told they paused the fight because of the arena ceiling cable that came down and the referee made a call to pause the match. After the fight ended they told us that the cable is 'part of the arena' and therefore they should have just let it play out and weren't supposed to call for a pause.|Seth Schaffer on Discord[https://discord.com/channels/651601084019900483/809971550937808926/1529962076426997871 Public comment by Seth Schaffer in the NHRL Discord server]}} |- |
